title: Guide: today, kept channels
note: v1.1: the morning after, an NBA studio show gets a quiet warning instead of its description, and the re-air of the hidden game shows no end time.

title: Guide: back in time
note: Hold ◀ to go back. Kept programmes look normal with the history mark; ESPN and CNN aren't kept (outlined). OK resumes Coastline.

title: Guide: last night's game
note: Shield on. Last night's game: description hidden, OK plays it from tip-off (not the pre-game). v1.1: line 2 names it the way the NBA pages do (Mon 26 Oct · late).

title: Guide: a channel that isn't kept
note: Back in time on a channel the provider doesn't keep: one outlined cell, still focusable so ▲▼ keep the time. OK tunes it live.

title: Home: the morning after
note: 10:40, shield My team. Last night's game is unseen and kept, so Home opens on it: Watch from tip-off is focused. No score, no record past the seen games.

title: Home: resume the replay
note: You stopped in Q3 last time. Resume (focused), From tip-off, Game page. The slab shows where you stopped; the card says "Stopped in Q3", never minutes left.

title: Home: live, from tip-off
note: 01:52, live. Watch live stays first; From tip-off sits next to it (one ▶). With three buttons the channel name moves to the status row.

title: NBA: yesterday, replays
note: A provider with no archive: the replay is a video in its Movies (matched by teams and date). Cards with a replay say so; the Grizzlies card stays hidden.

title: NBA: hold OK on a final
note: Hold OK on a final with a replay: Watch from tip-off first and focused. Reveal names its game and comes last. The menu opens beside the card: below it is off-screen, above it would touch the team plates.

title: Game page: hidden, replay
note: Shield on: the card in the body offers the replay first (focused). Reveal names the game and is a move away. Plays is dropped while hidden.

title: Game page: seen, watch again
note: Sun's game, seen: the box score as today, and Watch again at the right of the tab row. (Box score figures are illustrative.)

title: Game page: no replay
note: Neither an archive nor a video: say so plainly, keep looking every hour, and let you pick a video yourself. Look again is focused, never Reveal.

title: Choose a video
note: v1.1: the case you reach it in (nothing matched). Names that could tell the result are hidden whatever the shield mode; older and seen ones show.

title: Where to watch it from
note: Hold OK on Watch from tip-off: every source airglow found, best first and focused. OK plays it from tip-off.

title: Team page: schedule, replays
note: The schedule rail: finals you can still watch carry the history mark at the end of the result line. The Warriors game has dropped out of the 3-day archive.

title: Team page: hold OK on a tile
note: Hold OK on a tile with a replay: Watch from tip-off is first and focused; Reveal comes last. OK on the tile still opens the game page.

title: Player: from tip-off, game live
note: From tip-off on a live game: a fixed 3½ h window, the live point the red dot. v1.1: line 2 says where you are, never where live is; the Game button opens the panel.

title: Player: skip halftime
note: ▲ to the buttons at halftime: the skip reads "Skip halftime" and OK lands on the Q3 tip. The hint bar says what OK does.

title: Player: replay, shield on
note: A finished game under the shield: the bar never shows where it ends. v1.1: Back to live stays for the whole replay (under the shield it always asks first); a Game button.

title: Player: scrubbing a replay
note: Hold ▶: faster every second (×2 to ×32). The bubble names the quarter of the thumb, never past Q4; nothing on the bar changes until the picture plays there.

title: Player: quarters panel
note: The Game button in a replay: the game as aired, 90 s behind the picture, and the quarters to jump to. No box score, no OT row ahead.

title: Player: Options, live game
note: ◀ on a live game on a kept channel: Watch from tip-off is the second row (Sync score stays first), Rewind and pause the third. Two more rows below.

title: Player: Back to live, shield on
note: v1.1: under the shield, Back to live in a hidden game's replay always asks, with the same words, so the card never tells whether the game has ended.

title: Player: an archived programme
note: OK on a kept programme in the guide: the movie bar, with the programme's own times. At the end, Up next offers the next programme on the channel.

title: Player: live TV paused
note: Pause on a kept channel: the bar shows the programme, the live edge and how far behind you are. ⏮ starts the programme over; Back to live returns.

title: Player: paused, not kept
note: v1.1 (review M9): a channel the provider doesn't keep rewinds only inside the stream's own window (HLS, 45 s here); a .ts channel pauses only. The bar shows the real span.

title: Player: a full-game video
note: A video from Movies plays in the same hidden-end timeline (also when started from Movies). No quarter marks: its timing is unknown.

title: Player: the replay didn't start
note: If the archive fails, the other source is one OK away (here the video in Movies), focused. No score anywhere on the card.

title: Player: game panel, from tip-off
note: ▶ while watching a live game on a kept channel: the panel (the reveal you asked for, as today) gets a From tip-off button at its foot. v1.1: the tabs fit the panel (the Sync chip was cut). (Figures illustrative.)

title: Home: behind in a replay
note: v1.1 (review M3): 02:35, you left your replay in Q1. The game shows your position, never the live clock; LIVE stays until tip-off + 3 h 30; the channel keeps the game's title.

title: Player: Options in a replay
note: v1.1: ▼ in a game replay. Game panel (the panel's second way in, M8), Other sources, and Not the game? for a replay that lands on the wrong show (M6).

title: Player: Not the game?
note: v1.2: each row leads with what you can see, then what it does. One OK moves the replay and stores the correction per channel, applied to every later replay.

title: Player: one stream at a time
note: v1.1 (review S3): one of the split failure cards. Seeking asks once per pause in key presses (M10); if the provider still says the slot is taken, it waits and retries on its own.
